description:
A recording, which goes out without the user's Send, takes back a view's message the user left as it was. The agent has shown, in the conversation /c/{{SLUG}}, a page with output_html: "the view" is the frame ".output-iframe-tool iframe". Its button #send asks to send "echo: sent from the page" as the user's message, and #seal "echo: fw_ViewMadeToken12345678 from the page" (which looks like it holds an API key); both then show how that went in #sent. Name elements by ARIA role and accessible name, as Playwright's getByRole does; "named X" means an exact name match. "The consent bar" is data-testid "mcp-app-consent", where the host asks the user's OK for links and downloads a view asks for. "The text box" is data-testid "message-input", and "the draft label" data-testid "view-draft", which shows above the text box while it holds a message a view asked to send. To "send T": fill data-testid "message-input" with T and click data-testid "send-button". "The agent says T": the last ".message-agent" whose text contains T should be visible (timeout 30s). The page fakes the microphone, screen capture and MediaRecorder, and window.__recordingMock counts what the page asked for (read it with eval, e.g. "window.__recordingMock.recorderStarts"): displayRequests (screen captures requested), synchronousDisplayRequests (those requested inside a click or keydown handler), microphoneRequests, audioSources, recorderStarts, recorderStops and stoppedTracks (media tracks stopped). "The recording state" is the data-state attribute of ".recording-status". The voice button is [data-testid="voice-button"], the recording panel [data-testid="recording-panel"], and its cancel button [data-testid="recording-cancel-button"]. Perform the steps in order. 1. Navigate to /c/{{SLUG}}. Fill the text box with "Mine.". 2. Click the view's #send. Eval, in the page, document.querySelector('[data-testid="message-input"]').value === "Mine.

echo: sent from the page": it must return true. The draft label should be visible. 3. Click the voice button (a click step on its selector, not an eval). The recording panel should be visible, and window.__recordingMock.recorderStarts should become 1. [data-testid="recording-preserved-text"] should have exactly the text "Mine.", and the view's #sent exactly the text "The user declined.". 4. Click the cancel button. No recording panel should remain (count 0). The text box should have the value exactly "Mine.", and there should be no draft label (count 0). 5. Once the user edits, the text is theirs. Eval, in the view, (document.getElementById("sent").textContent = "", true): it must return true. Click the view's #send; the text box should have the value exactly "Mine.

echo: sent from the page". Eval, in the page, (() => { const box = document.querySelector('[data-testid="message-input"]'); box.focus(); box.setSelectionRange(0, 0); return true; })(): it must return true. Type "Oh. " (into the focused text box, at the start). Eval, in the page, document.querySelector('[data-testid="message-input"]').value === "Oh. Mine.

echo: sent from the page": it must return true. The draft label should be visible. 6. Click the voice button. window.__recordingMock.recorderStarts should become 2. [data-testid="recording-preserved-text"] should contain the text "echo: sent from the page", and the view's #sent should have exactly the text "The user declined.". 7. Click the cancel button. Eval, in the page, document.querySelector('[data-testid="message-input"]').value === "Oh. Mine.

echo: sent from the page": it must return true. There should be no draft label (count 0). 8. Nothing but the user changes the view's text, not even sealing what looks like a secret in it.
